intro.eyebrow: Kelly, Grammy and a family recipe
intro.title: Our Story
intro.lede: Native WILDFlour is a small, independent cafe on the corner of First Avenue and State Street in Skagway, Alaska. It starts with Kelly, her Grammy, and a passed-down family bannock recipe.

meetKelly.title: Meet Kelly
paragraphs: Kelly trained at the Culinary Art Institute in Seattle. Today she bakes and fries in Skagway, at a little counter one block west of Broadway, close enough to the water that you can walk over from the docks.
The bannock is fresh fried and made to order, one piece at a time. Alongside it she bakes cookies and muffins by hand and puts together a savory bannock lunch special that changes daily.
Nothing here is big or complicated: bread fried to order, baked goods made by hand, and a menu short enough to keep it that way.

grammy.title: Grammy’s kitchen
paragraphs: Ask Kelly where all of this comes from and the answer is her Grammy. Kelly calls her the greatest inspiration in her life.
Her love, generosity and recipes inspire everything Kelly makes.
grammy.quote: filled our hearts and tummies with the smell of fresh baking

recipe.title: The family bannock recipe
recipe.lead: Handed down through the family, and made to order every time.
recipe.intro: Every piece is fried to order, so it reaches you hot and golden. Then you choose how to finish it.
recipe.outro: The savory lunch specials rotate daily and often sell out, so it is worth coming early. Whatever is on today, it is posted on Facebook.

whatIsBannock.title: What is bannock?
paragraphs: Bannock is a simple, hearty bread — flour, water, a little fat and leavening — pan-fried or baked until golden. It is a beloved staple across Alaska Native and First Nations communities and throughout the North, and families pass down their own versions.
Ours is the Alaskan kind: fresh fried bread, made to order, served plain or under a spoonful of something sweet.

madeInSkagway.title: Made in Skagway
madeInSkagway.lead: Small, independent and open for the season.

cards.title: One little cafe
cards.body: No chain behind us. The person who owns Native WILDFlour is the person doing the baking.

cards.title: Open for the season
cards.body: Open for the summer cruise season — seasonal updates are posted on Facebook.

cards.title: Alaska-roasted coffee
cards.body: We proudly pour Kaladi Brothers Coffee, roasted in Alaska, alongside hot tea and cold drinks.

sayHello.title: Come say hello
sayHello.lead: We are a short walk from the cruise docks, at the south end of downtown Skagway.
